body:
So, I am ready to work on a new PR for directory formatting on Windows.
My take is that the double / (C://Windows) is a no brainer and should be fixed as a bug.

But should \ be preserved or replaced with /? 
(Powershell and cmd understand / or \ so it's really about what is "nicer" to the eye)

Even as a Windows addict for the last 25 years, I can say that, for me, / are better looking than \ in 2020. But, I'm really "open minded" on the matter.

TIL! I did not know that cmd and powershell accepted either '\\' or '/'.

To my mind, the best approach is always to follow idiomatic platform conventions wherever possible. So when in Windows land, I think the correct approach is to have the prompt display 'C:\Windows' because that's what cmd and Powrshell display when tab completing. 

Hope that makes sense!
Just to add to this discussion, when copy pasting paths in code, \ require you to double them most of the time ("c:\\Windows"), and / don't.
I'd also prefer `/` as the default, but I think it needs to be configurable.

A configuration setting? Why not. As long as the path displayed is valid, I'm all for it.
I have no experience with the addition of configuration option but can look it up.
À boolean? force_forward_slash?

Jean
I was thinking of something like `directory_seperator = "/"` and allowing any string, not limited to windows.

I'm fine with that.
Implies that users will be able to use "any" separator potentially leading to unwanted side effects but, you know, it's their configs! :-)
what about preferred_separator = "/" ?

Preferred feels redundant. The setting will likely end up part of the directory module, so how about just seperator?
Restricting the setting to char would make it less prone to unwanted side effects, but this would restrict the use of some emojis.

I have a working solution to implement this.
Now testing it for a couple of days and if it seems bullet proof, I'll submit a PR.

Reviewing the changes I made (and the changes to the tests), there is a bigger dependency in starship in the PWD environment variable (carrying the "logical" "shell dependent" path).
I would rather bring this via a command line argument (like --logical-path or --shell-path).
This would simplify the starship.ps1 and the invocation of starship would be:

                starship prompt --path=<system physical path> --logical-path=<shell path>

IMHO: this would clarify which is which and simplify directory.rs (and corresponding tests).

Opinions?
This seems reasonable to me.

I have a working implementation for --logical-path that I feel is cleaner, leaner, less "logic" error prone.
I will continue testing it for the next few days before submitting a new PR.
If anyone is interested, it can be found here: https://github.com/jeanga/starship/tree/jeanga/directory.
Maybe you could open a draft PR? BTW you can get the main seperator with `std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR`.

Okay! I will default the separator value with std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR 👍 
and will submit a draft PR (if I find how to create one ;-))

Sorry, I'm new to Rust and I struggle to find a better way to convert the char to str than:
    separator: if std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR == '\\' {"\\"} else {"/"},
`std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string()`? plain `.into()` might work too.

I implemented the DirectoryConfig's separator as str and not String... so to_string() did not work.
Neither did .into()...
`&std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string()`?
reference to a temporary value...

IIRC that could work
```
let a = std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string();
&a
```
Though if the seperator needs to leave the scope, it should be a `String`.

yeah. that is the conclusion I finally had too 👍 
Thank you for your help!
I love how Rust forces you to think of lifetimes!
(I come from a C++ background)

I looked at it and I think the config macro doesn't lhave handling for the `String` type.
Maybe use this to support the different separators I found on Wikipedia and get a warning if anything else ever gets supported.:
```rust
match std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR {
    '/' => "/",
    '\\' => "\\",
    '.' => ".",
    ':' => ":",
	'>' => ">",
    _ => panic!("Unknown Seperator"),
}
```
Ok, will do. Thank you for looking that up. Appreciated

Looking forward to this one for Nu.  The current starship does this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/547158/82496425-d14e4000-9b40-11ea-969f-4f06632db42d.png)

Being able to use the official Windows separator would be great.

Kinda solved by adding the following to your `starship.toml`

```
[directory.substitutions]
'/' = '\'
```

But I do think that Starship should still default to align with OS defaults.

I wonder if applying [`std::path::PathBuf::from_slash`](https://docs.rs/path-slash/0.1.4/path_slash/trait.PathBufExt.html#tymethod.from_slash) to the directory string after all the transformations (before/after adding the prefix?) would resolve this. I'm not sure of all the possible forms the `dir_string` can take...

I made an example PR of that in https://github.com/starship/starship/pull/3157, this is not a complete PR and breaks tests. The point is for someone more familiar with the project to look at it and and say if this is the right approach and if so, I or someone else can work on making this into a real PR. (e.g. Makes test/CI work, maybe put it under a setting, etc.)
